A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TempoControl and contain readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation; no material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original temporal-control experiments, loss ablations, qualitative generations, and a 50-participant user study in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds backbone comparisons, optimization ablations, alternative-objective comparisons, and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The attention aggregation, correlation/magnitude/entropy losses, latent optimization, and correlation-based stopping rule remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. The shorter optimization window is an experimental setting change; cosine similarity is tested as an ablation rather than adopted.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 80 object categories, 82 object pairs, 100 motion prompts, constant-presence VBench task, audio-alignment examples, and human-evaluation tasks. Added backbones and optimization experiments do not introduce different data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LTX-2 across all three tasks and CogX-S (2B) for one-object control. New appendix comparisons evaluate Dense Diffusion and a cosine-similarity variant against TempoControl. The earlier CogX1.5 (5B) comparator remains under the name CogX1.5-L.

E3.justification: The stated default changes from optimizing ten denoising steps to five, retaining up to ten gradient updates per step. New experiments vary optimization depth and update count and evaluate the method on CogX-S; existing task protocols and metrics remain. Exact update counts are inconsistent: Table 8 says five updates but repeats the 83.56% result labeled ten updates in Table 7.

E4.justification: v3 adds a latency–accuracy analysis, separate sweeps of gradient updates and optimized denoising steps across tasks/backbones, and a Pearson-versus-cosine objective ablation. These substantially extend the questions tested beyond the retained loss-weight, entropy-failure, and temporal-prompt analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance procedures. The retained human-study reporting does not introduce new uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces TempoControl's Wan temporal accuracies of 82.50%, 52.93%, and 57% with 83.56%, 53.17%, and 54% for one object, two objects, and movement, respectively. These accompany the shorter optimization window and are not same-setting gains. New results include CogX-S control, Dense Diffusion and cosine comparisons, and extensive latency/optimization measurements; the earlier human-study and VBench results remain.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–10 are substantively retained; the indicator notation in Equation 8 is merely restyled. No new theorem, proof, or formal derivation is introduced. The new objective comparisons provide conceptual explanations and empirical evidence.

C1.justification: The abstract and three stated contributions remain substantively unchanged. The conclusion modestly broadens the diagnosis from inadequate temporal text conditioning to claiming that temporal control is not a prompting problem and reflects a gap in temporal representation.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of latency saturation, when different backbones establish temporal structure, CogX-S failure conditions, and why direct masking or cosine alignment underperform. It extends the existing detector-failure discussion into a broader qualification of proxy-based evaluation. These are substantial additions to interpretation, although the experiments do not independently establish every proposed mechanism.

D1.justification: The reported GPU changes from H200 to B200, and v3 provides configuration-specific runtimes and additional optimization settings. It removes v2's disclosure that hyperparameters were tuned on small task-specific validation splits, without establishing that this practice stopped. Algorithmic pseudocode and project/code access statements remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kim et al.'s Dense text-to-image generation with attention modulation as reference 15 and explicitly positions TempoControl against its masking approach. The existing related-work discussion, including the distinction from MinT, is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v3 edits author/contact information, compresses parts of the quantitative and qualitative discussion, and rewrites the limitations and conclusion. New appendix sections are inserted around retained material. The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and overall narrative structure remain largely stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the latency plot in Figure 9 and five tables: Tables 5–8 and 11. Table 1 gains comparison rows, while Tables 1–3 receive revised grouped headers and captions. Existing qualitative figures and appendix tables are retained and mostly renumbered or relocated.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's controlled results on Wan and isolated runtime estimate, v3 offers useful evidence about portability, competing attention-control approaches, and computational tradeoffs. However, conflicting update counts in Tables 7–8 make the new optimization results harder to reproduce, and several added mechanism explanations exceed what the comparisons establish. The expanded evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than an unqualified substantial gain.
